meta_description: Kiln optimization on edge intelligence — specific fuel consumption down 6% and clinker quality variance down 22%

blocks.x: Kiln optimization on edge intelligence, specific fuel consumption down 6% and clinker quality variance down 22%

A cement producer: Plants feel data gaps in scrap rates and unplanned downtime, both traceable to decisions made hours earlier. The Achala program started at the line —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline quarter measured the flame: specific fuel consumption varying 9% between operators, clinker free-lime variance driving quality holds, and lab results arriving too late to correct the shift that caused them.
Recommendations from a vendor's black box had been tried and rejected, operators overrode what they couldn't see reasons for, and the override log was the most honest document on site.

We built the kiln twin with edge intelligence: process streams fused into a live thermal model at the plant edge (no cloud round-trip on the control loop), recommendations shown with their reasoning and expected delta, operators approving each setpoint move with overrides logged and learned from, and the lab loop shortened so quality data corrects its own shift.
